rows.notes: The cited study is a literature review (article type labelled 'Review'; Section 5 describes a keyword-based search of Google Scholar and Scopus yielding 22 articles that are classified in Tables 1-4). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or validated model runs. The 'model' in Section 6.4 and Fig. 1 is a conceptual scheme for combining RS, ML, soil indicators, climate and crop management data; the authors explicitly state that its validation must still be presented in a future case study. Hence it does not itself use RS and ML to estimate soil quality or enhance nutrient management; it only synthesises how others did so.

Same review paper, no primary data. The statement that the ML unit's production is used by crop management to adjust practices and thereby improve crop yield (Section 7, Fig. 1) is a description of a proposed conceptual framework, not a measured result; the authors note that none of the 22 reviewed studies report how the generated information was used by crop managers, and that validation of their model remains to be done in a case study. No evidence of its own on crop yield improvement.

notes: Document is a complete literature review (Ecological Indicators 135, 2022, 108517) of 22 studies using ML on remote-sensing data to estimate soil quality indicators; it proposes an untested conceptual model (Fig. 1) for local-scale soil quality estimation.
